Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.35% today to $363.54, recovering from yesterday's sharp 3.9% drop. The modest gain comes as refineries across the US are running at 97.4% capacity—near maximum utilization—which supports margins for refiners like Marathon. Oil prices remain elevated (US crude at $83.90/barrel), though geopolitical tensions that had been driving energy prices higher appear to be slightly cooling: Iran signaled today that a return to diplomacy "isn't impossible," and Qatar's prime minister is in Tehran for de-escalation talks.

The bigger picture here is that the Iran conflict has dragged on far longer than expected with no clear resolution, which had boosted crude prices and refiner profits through most of August. Today's small recovery and the diplomatic signals suggest investors may be pricing in slightly less extreme geopolitical risk, though the standoff remains unresolved and refinery utilization stays exceptionally high—both factors that have supported Marathon's stock over the past two weeks despite daily volatility.
